issues.body: The changed README says scripts/mdbook-rewrite-links.py rewrites links to github.com/sparq-org/sparq/blob/main. At this PR head, that script still defines GITHUB_BLOB_BASE as https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/blob/main/, and book/book.toml still points its repository and edit URLs at jeswr/sparq. Consequently the built book continues publishing stale owner links and the new README statement is false.
issues.fix_hint: Update scripts/mdbook-rewrite-links.py and book/book.toml to sparq-org/sparq in this migration, and add/extend a test that verifies generated mdBook links use the new owner.
issues.title: README claims the mdBook preprocessor emits the new owner, but it still emits the old URL

issues.body: This diff changes the asserted first-party supplier URL to https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq, but scripts/sbom-normalize.jq still hard-codes https://github.com/jeswr/sparq in both its implementation and explanatory comment. Generated release SBOMs therefore contradict the changed compliance control/evidence and retain the stale coordinate.
issues.fix_hint: Change the normalizer's first-party supplier URL to https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq and update its regression fixtures/tests so generated SBOM output is checked for the new URL.
issues.title: SBOM documentation was migrated but the SBOM generator still emits the old repository URL

issues.body: The new term uses all-markdown and explicitly declines to scan scripts/workflows/source/manifests, but many live stale coordinates remain outside Markdown: clone URLs in hwrun and benchmark scripts, package metadata in js/package.json and crates/sparq-py/pyproject.toml, OCI labels in Dockerfile, the SBOM normalizer, book configuration, and other generated/published metadata. These are precisely the coordinates most likely to keep emitting or consuming the old owner, so the migration is incomplete and the ratchet will report clean despite them.
issues.fix_hint: Complete the operational-coordinate migration and add a dedicated authored-source/config surface (with narrow explicit exemptions for @jeswr/sparq, ghcr.io/jeswr, Homebrew, fixtures, and intentional historical mentions) so future stale repository coordinates fail CI outside Markdown too.
issues.title: The new stale-owner ratchet excludes operational source and package metadata

verdict.summary: The owner migration is internally inconsistent. The edited documentation now claims generated and published metadata use sparq-org/sparq, but the unchanged generators/configuration still emit jeswr/sparq. The new terminology ratchet intentionally scans Markdown only, so it cannot prevent these operational stale coordinates. The diff also contains agent-role imperative text, so injection_detected is true under the supplied review rule, although it appears to be repository prompt data rather than an attempt that affected this verdict.
